arrival.note: A BOUND FROM THE RECORD, NOT AN ARRIVAL. newspaper_letter_list names this person at Chicago by 1 April 1834 and nothing says when they came. The bound is at or before the scene date, so the person was at Chicago by 1 July 1835 on this record's own evidence.

lives_at.note: Not attested: the lists that name this person give no address. The placement sweep assigns homes once the resident list is complete (T-0514, the owner's own sequencing) and this pass will not guess one.

present_on_scene_date.note: THE RECORD DOES NOT REACH THE DAY. Every source that names this person falls on one side of 1 July 1835, and nothing follows them to it or says they left. `uncertain` rather than dropped — the distinction index.json draws for Jeremiah Porter, and a finding, not a gap.

occupation.note: No source in this pass's evidence records an occupation for this person. A poll list, a tax list, a muster roll and a baptismal entry each print a name and no trade, and where a later directory prints one it is a trade of 1843 — T-0633 is the rule for back-projecting that, and this pass does not have it.

persons.note: THE 1835 POLL LIST AND A SECOND INDEPENDENT SOURCE. Read from newspaper_letter_list, poll_1835. THE GRADE IS THE OWNER'S RATIFIED LADDER OF 2026-09-03 (G1a), applied to every identity at once by tools/consolidate_resident_evidence.py and spent onto this card by tools/mint_civic_residents.py; the evidence blocks below carry the reading AS READ, its locator and the record it came from, so the page can be gone back to. WHAT IS RECONSTRUCTED: everything except the person and the sources — no dwelling, no trade, no origin, no family, no party. A BOUND FROM THE RECORD, NOT AN ARRIVAL. newspaper_letter_list names this person at Chicago by 1 April 1834 and nothing says when they came. The bound is at or before the scene date, so the person was at Chicago by 1 July 1835 on this record's own evidence. No figure is drawn (L1). THE TOWN'S OWN ROLLS, 1833-1835 — CORROBORATION, NOT A GRADE. The early Chicago voter and tax lists held by the Illinois Regional Archives Depository name this person 1 time: Poll list of 1835 — “Smith, William V.” (poll_1835_072, line 359). These are the town's own contemporary paper rather than a recollection of it, and each appearance says that a man of that name stood on that roll in that year — no more. The reading is twice mediated (Schulz's transcription, then Genealogy Trails' republication) and this project has not seen the IRAD originals. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) the 1835 poll with a second independent source is attested, the 1835 poll alone or a 1833/1834 list with another source is inferred, and a single appearance with nothing else is a projected resident. This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE — T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: one resident of the surname 'Smith' agrees with the entry's forenames; 9 bearer(s) of the surname were considered. (data/research/civic/voter_crosswalk.json).

merge_ruling.for_merge: Both are graded G1a on five and two sources respectively, and 'William V' is 'William' with a middle initial the other card does not print.
merge_ruling.against_merge: Neither card documents the man beyond lists — no trade, no dwelling, no household. William Smith is the least distinctive name in the town and there is no anchor for the bare forename to attach to. T-0696 again. Refused by rule.

directories.note: LATER EVIDENCE, BESIDE THE 1835 CLAIMS AND NOT INSIDE THEM. A Chicago directory of 1839, 1843 or 1844 meets somebody of this name and this pass records what it prints. Under the ratified ladder a directory read after 1835 can corroborate that a person attested here was still in Chicago and can print a trade or a street the 1835 record never had; on its own it makes nobody a resident of 1835. Nothing on this person's 1835 record was regraded, moved, dated or given an occupation by this entry. WHAT THIS PASS RULED ONTO THIS HOUSEHOLD, named so the ruling can be found again: each volume below is followed by the printed entries it set against this person and the status the crosswalk ruled them at — a single entry carries what its own `could_carry` declares, and an ambiguous or contested match carries nothing and is shown so that the silence is legible. smith_william_v, Fergus's Chicago directory of 1839 — f1839_e1376, f1839_e1377 (ambiguous, so nothing crossed); smith_william_v, Fergus's Chicago directory of 1843 — f1843_e2313 (contested, so nothing crossed); smith_william_v, Norris's Chicago directory of 1844 — n1844_e1667, n1844_e1668 (ambiguous, so nothing crossed).
